title: Emergence of Nanoscale Modulation in Liquid Crystals as a Result of Short-Range Order Parameter Condensation
abstract: The discovery of the twist-bend nematic phase in liquid crystals composed of bent-core and dimeric molecules has revealed an unexpected mechanism for the spontaneous formation of nanoscale periodic structures in soft condensed matter. Unlike conventional liquid-crystalline phases, the twist-bend phase exhibits a nanoscale heliconical modulation despite the absence of molecular chirality. In this note, dedicated to the late R. Meyer, we discuss a Landau phenomenological interpretation of this phenomenon. The central idea is that a short-range orientational order parameter undergoes condensation, giving rise to a heliconical structure characterized by a finite wave vector. We emphasize that the conventional nematic order is already long-ranged, whereas the additional order parameter describes local orientational correlations hidden within the nematic state. The resulting phase transition bears a close analogy to the de Gennes theory of the nematic--smectic-A transition. Fluctuation effects are expected to drive the transition weakly first order. The theory also predicts a new Goldstone mode associated with the spontaneously broken continuous symmetry of the heliconical state
summary: This theoretical work explains the emergence of nanoscale heliconical structures in liquid crystals by proposing that the transition is driven by the condensation of a short-range orientational order parameter. Using Landau theory, the authors show this mechanism is analogous to other known phase transitions, predicting the resulting modulated phase and associated Goldstone modes.
main_problem: The paper addresses the spontaneous formation of nanoscale periodic structures, specifically the heliconical modulation, observed in the twist-bend nematic phase of liquid crystals.
main_result: This modulation arises from the condensation of a secondary, short-range orientational order parameter ($\varphi$) at a finite wave vector ($\mathbf{q}_0$), rather than a simple loss of conventional nematic order.
method: The analysis employs a Landau phenomenological theory, drawing analogies to established phase transitions like the de Gennes nematic-smectic-A transition.
model_or_system: The system is liquid crystals (bent-core/dimeric molecules) exhibiting the N-NTB transition. The theory models the free energy using two order parameters: the long-range nematic director ($\mathbf{n}$) and the short-range correlation parameter ($\varphi$).
key_observables: Heliconical modulation pitch ($\Lambda = 2\pi/q_0$), the secondary order parameter ($\varphi$), and the associated Goldstone mode.
important_parameters: The wave vector $\mathbf{q}_0$, and parameters governing the effective potential (e.g., $\alpha,  eta$ in the chiral case).
main_assumptions: The theory assumes the transition is driven by the condensation of $\varphi$ and predicts the transition is weakly first-order due to fluctuation effects.
paper_structure: The paper develops the Landau theory by first establishing the role of the secondary order parameter $\varphi$ condensing at $\mathbf{q}_0$. It then analyzes the resulting heliconical structure, drawing parallels to known phase transitions and discussing the implications of fluctuation corrections.
why_interesting: The concept of a secondary, hidden order parameter condensing at a finite wave vector to drive a phase transition is a general mechanism in condensed matter physics, relevant to understanding modulated phases in complex systems.
